'''GV/3-series guardian droids''', also known as '''''Guardian''-class Droids''' and commonly referred to as '''Guardian droids''', were droids that resembled [[Dog/Legends|canines]]. They were made by [[Cybot Galactica/Legends|Cybot Galactica]] to act as security.

==Description==
The GV/3 Guardian was a four-legged [[Droid/Legends|droid]] designed to resemble domesticated guard animals that were common on [[Planet/Legends|planets]] throughout [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. The droid's head had [[Dog/Legends|canine]] features and it possessed [[Photoreceptor/Legends|photoreceptors]]<ref name="EGTD">''[[The Essential Guide to Droids]]''</ref> keyed for both the [[Human/Legends|Human]] range<ref name="GFT" /> and [[Infrared/Legends|infrared]], as well as [[Audio sensor/Legends|audio]] and [[Olfactory sensor/Legends|olfactory sensors]]. Its [[Grasper jaw|triple-reinforced jaw assembly]] held two rows of razor-sharp serrated [[Blade incisor|incisors]] that were capable of fully retracting into the maw.<ref name="EGTD" />

The droid's body was constructed of [[Plasteel/Legends|plasteel]], and was heavyset and powerful. GV/3s were strong enough to carry a standard Human on their back, and the hydraulically-powered [[Servomotor/Legends|servomotors]] in their legs were capable of outrunning a fleeing individual or pinning an intruder down. Each leg ended in three [[Durasteel/Legends|durasteel]] claws.<ref name="EGTD" />

A retractable [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] was hidden in a sealed compartment on the droid's belly, positioned between the two front legs. The weapon was usually set for [[Stun/Legends|stun]], especially for GV/3s that were used in residential households. Units that patrolled other locations, such as industrial facilities, rarely had their weapons set to stun. [[Solar collector/Legends|Solar collection panels]] were installed around the middle of the GV/3's torso, allowing the droid to store energy throughout the [[Standard day/Legends|day]]. This meant the GV/3 spent less time recharging than other droids.<ref name="EGTD" />

The GV/3's [[Personality matrix/Legends|personality programming]] was the equal of a particularly intelligent animal. The droid was incapable of speaking [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]], but could understand simple commands spoken in the [[Language/Legends|language]]. The GV/3 communicated instead with growls, roars, and yips which was infused with emotion.<ref name="EGTD" />

GV/3s had a preprogrammed loyalty imprint that ensured the unit was devoted to its owner.<ref name="EGTD" /> The droid obeyed its master and other designated individuals, such as family members. If their charges were threatened by attackers, the GV/3 would immediately move to defend them unless specifically ordered to stand down.<ref name="J14">{{JournalCite|14|Cynabar's Droid Datalog (article series)}}</ref> The imprint ensured that the droid would often sacrifice itself rather than allow its charges to come to harm.<ref name="EGTD" />

==Role==
[[File:GV3GuardianDroid2-FF63.png|thumb|left|A GV/3 Guardian droid]]
GV/3-series droids were appropriate units for a wide variety of jobs.<ref name="EGTD" /> They were particularly desirable as perimeter guards, being capable of patrolling selected areas without tiring.<ref name="GFT" /> They were commonly purchased by wealthy landowners who wanted them to protect their estates from intruders and trespassers. [[Scientist/Legends|Scientists]] and the military employed them as guard droids for secure installations such as [[Laboratory/Legends|laboratories]] and military facilities.<ref name="EGTD" />

Parents purchased GV/3 droids to act as companions for their [[Youngling/Legends|children]], taking advantage of unit's loyalty imprint to ensure it defended its charges.<ref name="EGTD" /> The droids were faithful and devoted friends, protecting children from strangers in the absence of their parents. Children who grew up with GV/3 Guardians were assured to be in safe "paws" and developed fond memories of their companion, all the while giving their parents peace of mind over the youngling's safety.<ref name="GFT" />

Because the GV/3 was designed as a terrifying attacker, special care was given to ensure that it did not injure the charges in their care. The blade incisors in the droid's jaw were retractable, and only deployed when the unit detected danger.<ref name="EGTD" /> GV/3 Guardians were also capable of acting as a tracker in case of a kidnapping, or for summoning assistance in times of need.<ref name="GFT" />

==History==
[[Cybot Galactica/Legends|Cybot Galactica]], well known for its [[Protocol droid/Legends|protocol droids]], sought to broaden its offerings by creating a new niche in the droid market. The GV/3-series was designed to fill the role of protector, companion, and friend to its owner. Upon release, the GV/3 sold strongly and benefitted from positive word-of-mouth recommendations. The popularity of the unit as a children's companion rose after a GV/3 was featured in the popular [[holo-series]] ''[[Revella's Journey: A Story of a Girl and Her Droid]]''. As a result, families soon made up the largest percentage of GV/3 buyers.<ref name="EGTD" />

Around the time of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], GV/3 Guardians found a new role in search and rescue operations following a widely publicized incident on the planet [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]]. A [[Corellian/Legends|Corellian]] SAR [[Squad/Legends|squad]] employed a GV/3 to assist in the rescue of four spelunkers who had been trapped in the [[Keen's Grotto/Legends|Keen's Grotto]] catacombs. After the successful rescue, Cybot Galactica began developing a modified version for dedicated use as search and rescue droid, incorporating enhanced detection [[Sensor/Legends|sensors]], an [[emergency transponder]], a [[Spotlight/Legends|spotlight]], and survival gear sealed in a weatherproof packet.<ref name="EGTD" />

Cybot Galactica manufactured a variant of the GV/3, the [[Guardian Mark II Droid]], during the Galactic Civil War.<ref name="GU12ET">{{SonyCite|url=players/news_archive.vm?id=68375&month=072009|text=Friday Feature &ndash; Game Update 12 -- Engineering Trader}}</ref> [[Zeb (Cynabar's Droid Datalog)|Zeb]], a customer and commentator on [[Cynabar's Droid Datalog]], owned a GV/3 that had been modified to operate as a [[Scout/Legends|scouting]] assistant. Zeb added sensors, tracking [[SkillWare]], and an [[automap]] to the droid. Another commentator, the [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] [[Rollo Morsai]], shared that another smuggler of his acquaintance had modified a GV/3 Guardian to act as a guard for his [[Freighter/Legends|freighter]]. The droid had its aggression amped up, fitted with combat SkillWare, and equipped with [[Metal/Legends|metal]] claws and fangs.<ref name="J14" />
